subject: Critical Thinking
title: The Gish Gallop: Drowning Opponents in Arguments
description: One-minute skill: The Gish Gallop: Drowning Opponents in Arguments.

hook.text: In a debate, one side fires 20 weak arguments in 2 minutes. The other side can only refute 3.

buildup.text: Named after creationist Duane Gish, who used the technique: overwhelm with quantity so your opponent can't address.

discovery.text: It exploits asymmetry: making a false claim takes 5 seconds. Properly refuting it takes 5 minutes.

twist.text: Brandolini's Law: 'The energy needed to refute BS is an order of magnitude greater than to produce it.' Online, this.

punchline.text: Twenty bad arguments don't add up to one good one.

quiz.question: What is the Gish Gallop debate technique?
options: Overwhelming opponents with many weak arguments so they can't refute them all

details.summary: The Gish Gallop floods a debate with so many arguments that the opponent cannot possibly address them all. Named after creationist Duane Gish, it wins by volume rather than quality.
details.whyItMatters: Recognizing the Gish Gallop prevents you from being overwhelmed and helps you focus on the opponent's strongest claim instead of chasing every point.
takeaways: The Gish Gallop substitutes quantity for quality
The counter-strategy is to identify the strongest claim and focus there
Audiences mistake unanswered points for conceded ones

faq.question: How do you counter a Gish Gallop during a live debate?
faq.answer: Name the tactic explicitly, then choose the opponent's single strongest argument and dismantle it thoroughly. Explain that addressing every weak point would reward the tactic itself.

faq.question: Why is the Gish Gallop so effective on audiences?
faq.answer: Audiences tend to interpret unanswered claims as conceded points. The sheer volume creates an impression of overwhelming evidence even when each individual argument is weak.
